title.narrative: Shelter a Hungry Farmer: A 3 Point Rights Based Agenda

description.narrative:
Overall, the project seeks to influence States to actively provide for agro-based economic development. This will greatly improve the livelihood of the poor who are majority in Africa, Kenya and Uganda in particular. The main strategy for this project is intensifying church involvement in advocating for change in policy and practice by states in support for Small Holder Farmers’ (SHFs) Rights who contribute over 70% of the food consumed in rural areas and urban centres globally. Further, support to SHFs has a direct positive impact not only on household income generation but also on improving the health of poor families.
The project has a three point agenda. First, it aims at increasing the voice, influence and visibility of SHFs in regional, national and international decision making processes. Further, the project seeks to address issues of women SHFs who constitute the majority in the sector. Secondly the project will advocate that the East African states increase budgetary allocations up to 10% of their national budget. In giving the lobbying public support JHC in collaboration with CJPC networks will organize SHFs into campaign solidarity groups, in order to develop priority areas for relevant State agencies for funding. The third agenda is to lobby national, regional and international bodies to create an environment where inward investments thrive. These actions are aimed at driving actualization of a pro-poor policy and practice environment, in which rights of SHFs are promoted.
